section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (a)
clause: Meeting this goal requires robust, reliable, repeatable, and standardized evaluations of AI systems, as well as policies, institutions, and, as appropriate, other mechanisms to test, understand, and mitigate risks from these systems before they are put to use.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (a)
clause: It also requires addressing AI systems’ most pressing security risks— including with respect to biotechnology, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, and other national security dangers—while navigating AI’s opacity and complexity.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (a)
clause: Testing and evaluations including post-deployment performance monitoring, will help ensure that AI systems function as intended, are resilient against misuse or dangerous modifications, are ethically developed operated in a secure manner and are compliant with applicable Federal laws and policies.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (a)
clause: Finally, my Administration will help develop effective labeling content provenance mechanisms, so that Americans are able to determine when content is generated using AI when it is not.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (a)
clause: These actions will provide a vital foundation for an approach that addresses AI’s risks without unduly reducing its benefits.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (b)
clause: Promoting responsible innovation, competition, and collaboration will allow the United States to lead in AI and unlock the technology’s potential to solve some of society’s most difficult challenges.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (b)
clause: This effort requires investments in AI-related education, training, development, research, and capacity, while simultaneously tackling novel intellectual property (IP) questions and other problems to protect inventors and creators.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (b)
clause: Across the Federal Government, my Administration will support programs to provide Americans the skills they need for the age of AI attract the world’s AI talent to our shores—not just to study, but to stay—so that the companies and technologies of the future are made in America.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (b)
clause: The Federal Government will promote a fair, open, and competitive ecosystem and marketplace for AI related technologies so that small developers and entrepreneurs can continue to drive innovation.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (b)
clause: Doing so requires stopping unlawful collusion and addressing risks from dominant firms’ use of key assets such as semiconductors, computing power, cloud storage and data to disadvantage competitors and it requires supporting a marketplace that harnesses the benefits of AI to provide new opportunities for small businesses, workers and entrepreneurs.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (c)
clause: The responsible development and use of AI require a commitment to supporting American workers.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (c)
clause: As AI creates new jobs and industries, all workers need a seat at the table including through collective bargaining, to ensure that they benefit from these opportunities.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (c)
clause: My Administration will seek to adapt job training education to support a diverse workforce and help provide access to opportunities that AI creates.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (c)
clause: In the workplace itself, AI should not be deployed in ways that undermine rights, worsen job quality, encourage undue worker surveillance, lessen market competition, introduce new health and safety risks, or cause harmful labor-force disruptions.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (c)
clause: The critical next steps in AI development should be built on the views of workers, labor unions, educators and employers to support responsible uses of AI that improve workers’ lives, positively augment human work and help all people safely enjoy the gains and opportunities from technological innovation.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: Artificial Intelligence policies must be consistent with my Administration’s dedication to advancing equity and civil rights.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: My Administration cannot—and will not—tolerate the use of AI to disadvantage those who are already too often denied equal opportunity and justice.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: From hiring to housing to healthcare, we have seen what happens when AI use deepens discrimination and bias, rather than improving quality of life.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: Artificial Intelligence systems deployed irresponsibly have reproduced intensified existing inequities, caused new types of harmful discrimination, and exacerbated online and physical harms.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: My Administration will build on the important steps that have already been taken—such as issuing the Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights, the AI Risk Management Framework, and Executive Order 14091 of February 16, 2023 (Further Advancing Racial Equity

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government)— in seeking to ensure that AI complies with all Federal laws to promote robust technical evaluations, careful oversight, engagement with affected communities, and rigorous regulation.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: It is necessary to hold those developing and deploying AI accountable to standards that protect against unlawful discrimination and abuse including in the justice system and the Federal Government.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (d)
clause: Only then can Americans trust AI to advance civil rights, civil liberties, equity, and justice for all.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (e)
clause: The interests of Americans who increasingly use, interact with, or purchase AI and AI-enabled products in their daily lives must be protected.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (e)
clause: Use of new technologies, such as AI, does not excuse organizations from their legal obligations, and hard-won consumer protections are more important than ever in moments of technological change.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (e)
clause: The Federal Government will enforce existing consumer protection laws principles enact appropriate safeguards against fraud, unintended bias, discrimination, infringements on privacy, and other harms from AI.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (e)
clause: Such protections are especially important in critical fields like healthcare, financial services, education, housing, law, and transportation, where mistakes by or misuse of AI could harm patients, cost consumers or small businesses, or jeopardize safety or rights.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan
clause: At the same time, my Administration will promote responsible uses of AI that protect consumers, raise the quality of goods and services, lower their prices, or expand selection and availability.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (f)
clause: Americans’ privacy civil liberties must be protected as AI continues advancing.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (f)
clause: Artificial Intelligence is making it easier to extract, re-identify, link, infer, and act on sensitive information about people’s identities, locations, habits, and desires.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (f)

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (f)
clause: To combat this risk, the Federal Government will ensure that the collection, use, and retention of data is lawful, is secure, and mitigates privacy and confidentiality risks.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (f)
clause: Agencies shall use available policy and technical tools including privacy-enhancing technologies (PETs) where appropriate, to protect privacy to combat the broader legal and societal risks—including the chilling of First Amendment rights—that result from the improper collection and use of people’s data.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (g)
clause: It is important to manage the risks from the Federal Government’s own use of AI and increase its internal capacity to regulate, govern, and support responsible use of AI to deliver better results for Americans.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (g)
clause: These efforts start with people, our Nation’s greatest asset.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (g)
clause: My Administration will take steps to attract, retain, and develop public service-oriented AI professionals including from underserved communities, across disciplines— including technology, policy, managerial, procurement, regulatory, ethical, governance, and legal fields—and ease AI professionals’ path into the Federal Government to help harness and govern AI.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (g)
clause: The Federal Government will work to ensure that all members of its workforce receive adequate training to understand the benefits, risks and limitations of AI for their job functions and to modernize Federal Government information technology infrastructure, remove bureaucratic obstacles and ensure that safe and rights-respecting AI is adopted, deployed

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (h)
clause: The Federal Government should lead the way to global societal, economic, and technological progress, as the United States has in previous eras of disruptive innovation and change.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (h)
clause: This leadership is not measured solely by the technological advancements our country makes.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (h)
clause: Effective leadership also means pioneering those systems safeguards needed to deploy technology responsibly—and building and promoting those safeguards with the rest of the world.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (h)
clause: My Administration will engage with international allies and partners in developing a framework to manage AI’s risks, unlock AI’s potential for good, and promote common approaches to shared challenges.

source_full: Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
section: Sec. 2 . _Policy and Principles._ It is the policy of my Administration to advan > (h)
clause: The Federal Government will seek to promote responsible AI safety and security principles and actions with other nations including our competitors, while leading key global conversations and collaborations to ensure that AI benefits the whole world, rather than exacerbating inequities, threatening human rights, and causing other harms.

clause: Fig. 1 Examples of potential harms related to AI systems. Trustworthy AI systems and their responsible use can mitigate negative risks and contribute to benefits for people, organizations, and ecosystems.

clause: Ideally, risk management efforts start with the Plan and Design function in the application context. are performed throughout the AI system lifecycle. See Figure 3 for representative AI actors.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies have significant potential to transform society and people’s lives – from commerce and health to transportation and cybersecurity to the environment and our planet.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI technologies can drive inclusive economic growth support scientific advancements that improve the conditions of our world.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI technologies, however, also pose risks that can negatively impact individuals, groups, organizations, communities, society, the environment, and the planet.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Like risks for other types of technology, AI risks can emerge in a variety of ways can be characterized as long- or short-term, highor low-probability, systemic or localized, and high- or low-impact.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The AI RMF refers to an _AI system_ as an engineered or machine-based system that can, for a given set of objectives, generate outputs such as predictions, recommendations and decisions influencing real or virtual environments. AI systems are designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy (Adapted from: OECD Recommendation on AI:2019

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While there are myriad standards best practices to help organizations mitigate the risks of traditional software or information-based systems, the risks posed by AI systems are in many ways unique (See Appendix B).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems, for example, may be trained on data that can change over time, sometimes significantly and unexpectedly, affecting system functionality and trustworthiness in ways that are hard to understand.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems and the contexts in which they are deployed are frequently complex, making it difficult to detect and respond to failures when they occur.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems are inherently socio-technical in nature meaning they are influenced by societal dynamics and human behavior.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risk management offers a path to minimize potential negative impacts of AI systems, such as threats to civil liberties and rights, while also providing opportunities to maximize positive impacts. Addressing, documenting and managing AI risks and potential negative impacts effectively can lead to more trustworthy AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In the context of the AI RMF, _risk_ refers to the composite measure of an event’s probability of occurring and the magnitude or degree of the consequences of the corresponding event.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The impacts, or consequences, of AI systems can be positive, negative, or both can result in opportunities or threats (Adapted from: ISO 31000:2018).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: When considering the negative impact of a potential event, risk is a function of 1) the negative impact, or magnitude of harm, that would arise if the circumstance or event occurs and 2) the likelihood of occurrence (Adapted from: OMB Circular A-130:2016).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Negative impact or harm can be experienced by individuals, groups, communities, organizations, society, the environment, and the planet.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While risk management processes generally address negative impacts, this Framework offers approaches to minimize anticipated negative impacts of AI systems _and_ identify opportunities to maximize positive impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Effectively managing the risk of potential harms could lead to more trustworthy AI systems and unleash potential benefits to people (individuals, communities, and society), organizations, and systems/ecosystems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk management can enable AI developers and users to understand impacts account for the inherent limitations and uncertainties in their models and systems, which in turn can improve overall system performance and trustworthiness the likelihood that AI technologies will be used in ways that are beneficial.

clause: The AI RMF is designed to address new risks as they emerge.

clause: This flexibility is particularly important where impacts are not easily foreseeable and applications are evolving.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 1.2 Challenges for AI Risk Management

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Several challenges are described below. They should be taken into account when managing risks in pursuit of AI trustworthiness.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risks or failures that are not well-defined or adequately understood are difficult to measure quantitatively or qualitatively. The inability to appropriately measure AI risks does not imply that an AI system necessarily poses either a high or low risk. Some risk measurement challenges include:

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risks related to third-party software, hardware, and data: Third-party data or systems can accelerate research development and facilitate technology transition.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: They also may complicate risk measurement.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk can emerge both from third-party data, software or hardware itself how it is used.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk metrics or methodologies used by the organization developing the AI system may not align with the risk metrics or methodologies uses by the organization _deploying or operating_ the system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Also, the organization developing the AI system may not be transparent about the risk metrics or methodologies it used.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk measurement management can be complicated by how customers use or integrate thirdparty data or systems into AI products or services, particularly without sufficient internal governance structures and technical safeguards.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Regardless, all parties and AI actors should manage risk in the AI systems they develop, deploy, or use as standalone or integrated components.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI system impact assessment approaches can help AI actors understand potential impacts or harms within specific contexts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Availability of reliable metrics: The current lack of consensus on robust verifiable measurement methods for risk and trustworthiness, and applicability to different AI use cases, is an AI risk measurement challenge.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Potential pitfalls when seeking to measure negative risk or harms include the reality that development of metrics is often an institutional endeavor may inadvertently reflect factors unrelated to the underlying impact.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In addition, measurement approaches can be oversimplified, gamed, lack critical nuance, become relied upon in unexpected ways, or fail to account for differences in affected groups and contexts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk at different stages of the AI lifecycle: Measuring risk at an earlier stage in the AI lifecycle may yield different results than measuring risk at a later stage; some risks may be latent at a given point in time may increase as AI systems adapt and evolve.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Furthermore, different AI actors across the AI lifecycle can have different risk perspectives.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, an AI developer who makes AI software available, such as pre-trained models, can have a different risk perspective than an AI actor who is responsible for deploying that pre-trained model in a specific use case.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Such deployers may not recognize that their particular uses could entail risks which differ from those perceived by the initial developer.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: All involved AI actors share responsibilities for designing, developing, and deploying a trustworthy AI system that is fit for purpose.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk in real-world settings: While measuring AI risks in a laboratory or a controlled environment may yield important insights pre-deployment, these measurements may differ from risks that emerge in operational, real-world settings.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Inscrutability: Inscrutable AI systems can complicate risk measurement. Inscrutability can be a result of the opaque nature of AI systems (limited explainability or interpretability), lack of transparency or documentation in AI system development or deployment and inherent uncertainties in AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human baseline: Risk management of AI systems that are intended to augment or replace human activity, for example decision making, requires some form of baseline metrics for comparison. This is difficult to systematize since AI systems carry out different tasks – and perform tasks differently – than humans.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While the AI RMF can be used to prioritize risk, it does not prescribe risk tolerance. _Risk tolerance_ refers to the organization’s or AI actor’s (see Appendix A) readiness to bear the risk in order to achieve its objectives.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk tolerance can be influenced by legal or regulatory requirements (Adapted from: ISO GUIDE 73).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk tolerance and the level of risk that is acceptable to organizations or society are highly contextual and application and use-case specific.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk tolerances can be influenced by policies norms established by AI system owners, organizations, industries, communities, or policy makers.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk tolerances are likely to change over time as AI systems, policies, and norms evolve.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Different organizations may have varied risk tolerances due to their particular organizational priorities and resource considerations.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Emerging knowledge and methods to better inform harm/cost-benefit tradeoffs will continue to be developed debated by businesses, governments, academia, and civil society. To the extent that challenges for specifying AI risk tolerances remain unresolved, there may be contexts where a risk management framework is not yet readily applicable for mitigating negative AI risks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The Framework is intended to be flexible to augment existing risk practices which should align with applicable laws, regulations, and norms.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Organizations should follow existing regulations and guidelines for risk criteria, tolerance, and response established by organizational, domain, discipline, sector, or professional requirements.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Some sectors or industries may have established definitions of harm or established documentation, reporting, and disclosure requirements.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Within sectors, risk management may depend on existing guidelines for specific applications and use case settings.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Where established guidelines do not exist, organizations should define reasonable risk tolerance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Once tolerance is defined, this AI RMF can be used to manage risks to document risk management processes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Attempting to eliminate negative risk entirely can be counterproductive in practice because not all incidents and failures can be eliminated.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Unrealistic expectations about risk may lead organizations to allocate resources in a manner that makes risk triage inefficient or impractical or wastes scarce resources.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: A risk management culture can help organizations recognize that not all AI risks are the same, and resources can be allocated purposefully.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Actionable risk management efforts lay out clear guidelines for assessing trustworthiness of each AI system an organization develops or deploys.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Policies and resources should be prioritized based on the assessed risk level potential impact of an AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The extent to which an AI system may be customized or tailored to the specific context of use by the AI deployer can be a contributing factor.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: When applying the AI RMF, risks which the organization determines to be highest for the AI systems within a given context of use call for the most urgent prioritization most thorough risk management process.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In cases where an AI system presents unacceptable negative risk levels – such as where significant negative impacts are imminent, severe harms are actually occurring, or catastrophic risks are present – development deployment should cease in a safe manner until risks can be sufficiently managed.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: If an AI system’s development, deployment, and use cases are found to be low-risk in a specific context, that may suggest potentially lower prioritization.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk prioritization may differ between AI systems that are designed or deployed to directly interact with humans as compared to AI systems that are not.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Higher initial prioritization may be called for in settings where the AI system is trained on large datasets comprised of sensitive or protected data such as personally identifiable information, or where the outputs of the AI systems have direct or indirect impact on humans.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems designed to interact only with computational systems trained on non-sensitive datasets (for example, data collected from the physical environment) may call for lower initial prioritization.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Nonetheless, regularly assessing prioritizing risk based on context remains important because non-human-facing AI systems can have downstream safety or social implications.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Residual risk_ – defined as risk remaining after risk treatment (Source: ISO GUIDE 73) – directly impacts end users or affected individuals and communities. Documenting residual risks will call for the system provider to fully consider the risks of deploying the AI product will inform end users about potential negative impacts of interacting with the system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risks should not be considered in isolation.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Different AI actors have different responsibilities and awareness depending on their roles in the lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, organizations developing an AI system often will not have information about how the system may be used.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risk management should be integrated incorporated into broader enterprise risk management strategies and processes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Treating AI risks along with other critical risks, such as cybersecurity and privacy, will yield a more integrated outcome and organizational efficiencies.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The AI RMF may be utilized along with related guidance and frameworks for managing AI system risks or broader enterprise risks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Some risks related to AI systems are common across other types of software development and deployment.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Examples of overlapping risks include: privacy concerns related to the use of underlying data to train AI systems

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: the energy environmental implications associated with resource-heavy computing demands

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: security concerns related to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the system and its training output data

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: and general security of the underlying software and hardware for AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Organizations need to establish and maintain the appropriate accountability mechanisms, roles and responsibilities, culture, and incentive structures for risk management to be effective.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Use of the AI RMF alone will not lead to these changes or provide the appropriate incentives.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Effective risk management is realized through organizational commitment at senior levels may require cultural change within an organization or industry.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In addition, small to medium-sized organizations managing AI risks or implementing the AI RMF may face different challenges than large organizations, depending on their capabilities and resources.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Identifying and managing AI risks and potential impacts – both positive and negative – requires a broad set of perspectives and actors across the AI lifecycle. Ideally, AI actors will represent a diversity of experience, expertise and backgrounds and comprise demographically and disciplinarily diverse teams. The AI RMF is intended to be used by AI actors across the AI lifecycle and dimensions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 3. AI Risks and Trustworthiness

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For AI systems to be trustworthy, they often need to be responsive to a multiplicity of criteria that are of value to interested parties.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Approaches which enhance AI trustworthiness can reduce negative AI risks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: This Framework articulates the following characteristics of trustworthy AI and offers guidance for addressing them.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Characteristics of trustworthy AI systems include: valid and reliable, safe, secure and resilient, accountable and transparent, explainable and interpretable, privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Creating trustworthy AI requires balancing each of these characteristics based on the AI system’s context of use.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While all characteristics are socio-technical system attributes, accountability and transparency also relate to the processes and activities internal to an AI system and its external setting.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Neglecting these characteristics can increase the probability and magnitude of negative consequences.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Fig. 4. Characteristics of trustworthy AI systems. Valid & Reliable is a necessary condition of trustworthiness is shown as the base for other trustworthiness characteristics. Accountable & Transparent is shown as a vertical box because it relates to all other characteristics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Trustworthiness characteristics (shown in Figure 4) are inextricably tied to social and organizational behavior

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: the datasets used by AI systems, selection of AI models and algorithms and the decisions made by those who build them, and the interactions with the humans who provide insight from oversight of such systems. Human judgment should be employed when deciding on the specific metrics related to AI trustworthiness characteristics and the precise threshold values for those metrics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Addressing AI trustworthiness characteristics individually will not ensure AI system trustworthiness tradeoffs are usually involved, rarely do all characteristics apply in every setting, and some will be more or less important in any given situation. Ultimately, trustworthiness is a social concept that ranges across a spectrum is only as strong as its weakest characteristics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: When managing AI risks, organizations can face difficult decisions in balancing these characteristics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, in certain scenarios tradeoffs may emerge between optimizing for interpretability and achieving privacy.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In other cases, organizations might face a tradeoff between predictive accuracy and interpretability.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Or, under certain conditions such as data sparsity, privacy-enhancing techniques can result in a loss in accuracy, affecting decisions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: There are multiple approaches for enhancing contextual awareness in the AI lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, subject matter experts can assist in the evaluation of TEVV findings work with product deployment teams to align TEVV parameters to requirements deployment conditions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: When properly resourced, increasing the breadth diversity of input from interested parties relevant AI actors throughout the AI lifecycle can enhance opportunities for informing contextually sensitive evaluations, and for identifying AI system benefits and positive impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These practices can increase the likelihood that risks arising in social contexts are managed appropriately.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Understanding treatment of trustworthiness characteristics depends on an AI actor’s particular role within the AI lifecycle. For any given AI system, an AI designer or developer may have a different perception of the characteristics than the deployer.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Trustworthiness characteristics explained in this document influence each other.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Highly secure but unfair systems, accurate but opaque and uninterpretable systems, and inaccurate but secure, privacy-enhanced, and transparent systems are all undesirable.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: A comprehensive approach to risk management calls for balancing tradeoffs among the trustworthiness characteristics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: It is the joint responsibility of all AI actors to determine whether AI technology is an appropriate or necessary tool for a given context or purpose, and how to use it responsibly.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The decision to commission or deploy an AI system should be based on a contextual assessment of trustworthiness characteristics and the relative risks, impacts, costs, and benefits, and informed by a broad set of interested parties.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Validation_ is the “confirmation, through the provision of objective evidence, that the requirements for a specific intended use or application have been fulfilled” (Source: ISO 9000:2015). Deployment of AI systems which are inaccurate, unreliable, or poorly generalized to data and settings beyond their training creates and increases negative AI risks and reduces trustworthiness.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Reliability_ is defined in the same standard as the “ability of an item to perform as required, without failure, for a given time interval, under given conditions” (Source: ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Reliability is a goal for overall correctness of AI system operation under the conditions of expected use. over a given period of time including the entire lifetime of the system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Accuracy and robustness contribute to the validity and trustworthiness of AI systems and can be in tension with one another in AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Accuracy_ is defined by ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022 as “closeness of results of observations, computations and estimates to the true values or the values accepted as being true.” Measures of accuracy should consider computational-centric measures (e.g., false positive and false negative rates), human-AI teaming and demonstrate external validity (generalizable beyond the training conditions).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Accuracy measurements should always be paired with clearly defined realistic test sets – that are representative of conditions of expected use – and details about test methodology; these should be included in associated documentation.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Accuracy measurements may include disaggregation of results for different data segments.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Robustness_ or _generalizability_ is defined as the “ability of a system to maintain its level of performance under a variety of circumstances” (Source: ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Robustness is a goal for appropriate system functionality in a broad set of conditions and circumstances including uses of AI systems not initially anticipated.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Robustness requires not only that the system perform exactly as it does under expected uses, but also that it should perform in ways that minimize potential harms to people if it is operating in an unexpected setting. reliability for deployed AI systems are often assessed by ongoing testing or monitoring that confirms a system is performing as intended.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Measurement of validity, accuracy, robustness, and reliability contribute to trustworthiness should take into consideration that certain types of failures can cause greater harm.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risk management efforts should prioritize the minimization of potential negative impacts and may need to include human intervention in cases where the AI system cannot detect or correct errors.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems should “not under defined conditions, lead to a state in which human life, health, property, or the environment is endangered” (Source: ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022). Safe operation of AI systems is improved through:

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Different types of safety risks may require tailored AI risk management approaches based on context and the severity of potential risks presented. Safety risks that pose a potential risk of serious injury or death call for the most urgent prioritization most thorough risk management process.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Employing safety considerations during the lifecycle and starting as early as possible with planning design can prevent failures or conditions that can render a system dangerous. Other practical approaches for AI safety often relate to rigorous simulation and in-domain testing, real-time monitoring, and the ability to shut down, modify or have human intervention into systems that deviate from intended or expected functionality.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI safety risk management approaches should take cues from efforts and guidelines for safety in fields such as transportation and healthcare, and align with existing sector- or application-specific guidelines or standards.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems, as well as the ecosystems in which they are deployed, may be said to be _resilient_ if they can withstand unexpected adverse events or unexpected changes in their environment or use – or if they can maintain their functions and structure in the face of internal and external change and degrade safely gracefully when this is necessary (Adapted from: ISO/IEC TS 5723:2022).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Common security concerns relate to adversarial examples, data poisoning, and the exfiltration of models, training data, or other intellectual property through AI system endpoints.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems that can maintain confidentiality, integrity, and availability through protection mechanisms that prevent unauthorized access and use may be said to be _secure_ .

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Guidelines in the NIST Cybersecurity Framework

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk Management Framework are among those which are applicable here.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Trustworthy AI depends upon accountability.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Accountability presupposes transparency. _Transparency_ reflects the extent to which information about an AI system and its outputs is available to individuals interacting with such a system – regardless of whether they are even aware that they are doing so.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Meaningful transparency provides access to appropriate levels of information based on the stage of the AI lifecycle tailored to the role or knowledge of AI actors or individuals interacting with or using the AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: By promoting higher levels of understanding, transparency increases confidence in the AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: This characteristic’s scope spans from design decisions and training data to model training

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: the structure of the model, its intended use cases, and how when deployment, post-deployment, or end user decisions were made and by whom. Transparency is often necessary for actionable redress related to AI system outputs that are incorrect or otherwise lead to negative impacts. Transparency should consider human-AI interaction

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: for exam- ple, how a human operator or user is notified when a potential or actual adverse outcome caused by an AI system is detected. A transparent system is not necessarily an accurate, privacy-enhanced, secure and fair system. However, it is difficult to determine whether an opaque system possesses such characteristics and to do so over time as complex systems evolve.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The role of AI actors should be considered when seeking accountability for the outcomes of AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The relationship between risk accountability associated with AI and technological systems more broadly differs across cultural, legal, sectoral, and societal contexts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: When consequences are severe, such as when life liberty are at stake, AI developers and deployers should consider proportionally and proactively adjusting their transparency and accountability practices.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Maintaining organizational practices and governing structures for harm reduction, like risk management, can help lead to more accountable systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Maintaining the provenance of training data and supporting attribution of the AI system’s decisions to subsets of training data can assist with both transparency and accountability. Training data may also be subject to copyright should follow applicable intellectual property rights laws.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: As transparency tools for AI systems related documentation continue to evolve, developers of AI systems are encouraged to test different types of transparency tools in cooperation with AI deployers to ensure that AI systems are used as intended.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Explainability_ refers to a representation of the mechanisms underlying AI systems’ operation, whereas _interpretability_ refers to the meaning of AI systems’ output in the context of their designed functional purposes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Together, explainability interpretability assist those operating or overseeing an AI system, as well as users of an AI system, to gain deeper insights into the functionality and trustworthiness of the system including its outputs.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The underlying assumption is that perceptions of negative risk stem from a lack of ability to make sense of, or contextualize, system output appropriately.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Explainable and interpretable AI systems offer information that will help end users understand the purposes potential impact of an AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk from lack of explainability may be managed by describing how AI systems function, with descriptions tailored to individual differences such as the user’s role, knowledge, and skill level. Explainable systems can be debugged monitored more easily, and they lend themselves to more thorough documentation, audit, and governance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risks to interpretability often can be addressed by communicating a description of why an AI system made a particular prediction or recommendation. (See “Four Principles of Explainable Artificial Intelligence” and “Psychological Foundations of Explainability and Interpretability in Artificial Intelligence” found here.)

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Privacy_ refers generally to the norms practices that help to safeguard human autonomy, identity and dignity. These norms and practices typically address freedom from intrusion, limiting observation and individuals’ agency to consent to disclosure or control of facets of their identities (e.g., body, data, reputation). (See The NIST Privacy Framework

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: A Tool for Improving Privacy through Enterprise Risk Management.)

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Privacy values such as anonymity, confidentiality, and control generally should guide choices for AI system design, development, and deployment.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Privacy-related risks may influence security, bias, and transparency and come with tradeoffs with these other characteristics.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Like safety and security, specific technical features of an AI system may promote or reduce privacy.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems can also present new risks to privacy by allowing inference to identify individuals or previously private information about individuals.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Privacy-enhancing technologies (“PETs”) for AI, as well as data minimizing methods such as de-identification and aggregation for certain model outputs, can support design for privacy-enhanced AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Under certain conditions such as data sparsity, privacyenhancing techniques can result in a loss in accuracy, affecting decisions about fairness and other values in certain domains.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: _Fairness_ in AI includes concerns for equality and equity by addressing issues such as harmful bias and discrimination.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Standards of fairness can be complex difficult to define because perceptions of fairness differ among cultures may shift depending on application.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Organizations’ risk management efforts will be enhanced by recognizing and considering these differences.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Systems in which harmful biases are mitigated are not necessarily fair.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, systems in which predictions are somewhat balanced across demographic groups may still be inaccessible to individuals with disabilities or affected by the digital divide or may exacerbate existing disparities or systemic biases.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Bias is broader than demographic balance and data representativeness.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: NIST has identified three major categories of AI bias to be considered and managed: systemic, computational and statistical, and human-cognitive.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Each of these can occur in the absence of prejudice, partiality, or discriminatory intent.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Systemic bias can be present in AI datasets, the organizational norms, practices, and processes across the AI lifecycle, and the broader society that uses AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Computational and statistical biases can be present in AI datasets and algorithmic processes, and often stem from systematic errors due to non-representative samples.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human-cognitive biases relate to how an individual or group perceives AI system information to make a decision or fill in missing information, or how humans think about purposes and functions of an AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human-cognitive biases are omnipresent in decision-making processes across the AI lifecycle and system use including the design, implementation, operation, and maintenance of AI.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Bias exists in many forms can become ingrained in the automated systems that help make decisions about our lives.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While bias is not always a negative phenomenon, AI systems can potentially increase the speed and scale of biases and perpetuate and amplify harms to individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Bias is tightly associated with the concepts of transparency as well as fairness in society. (For more information about bias including the three categories, see NIST Special Publication 1270, Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence.)

clause: 4. Effectiveness of the AI RMF

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Evaluations of AI RMF effectiveness – including ways to measure bottom-line improvements in the trustworthiness of AI systems – will be part of future NIST activities, in conjunction with the AI community.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Organizations and other users of the Framework are encouraged to periodically evaluate whether the AI RMF has improved their ability to manage AI risks including but not limited to their policies, processes, practices, implementation plans, indicators, measurements, and expected outcomes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: NIST intends to work collaboratively with others to develop metrics, methodologies, and goals for evaluating the AI RMF’s effectiveness, and to broadly share results and supporting information.

clause: 5. AI RMF Core

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The AI RMF Core provides outcomes actions that enable dialogue, understanding, and activities to manage AI risks and responsibly develop trustworthy AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: As illustrated in Figure 5, the Core is composed of four functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE .

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Each of these high-level functions is broken down into categories and subcategories.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Categories subcategories are subdivided into specific actions and outcomes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Actions do not constitute a checklist, nor are they necessarily an ordered set of steps.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Fig. 5. Functions organize AI risk management activities at their highest level to govern, map, measure, and manage AI risks. Governance is designed to be a cross-cutting function to inform be infused throughout the other three functions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Risk management should be continuous, timely and performed throughout the AI system lifecycle dimensions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI RMF Core functions should be carried out in a way that reflects diverse and multidisciplinary perspectives, potentially including the views of AI actors outside the organization.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Like the AI RMF, the Playbook is voluntary and organizations can utilize the suggestions according to their needs and interests.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Playbook users can create tailored guidance selected from suggested material for their own use and contribute their suggestions for sharing with the broader community.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Strong governance can drive and enhance internal practices and norms to facilitate organizational risk culture.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Governing authorities can determine the overarching policies that direct an organization’s mission, goals, values, culture, and risk tolerance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Senior leadership sets the tone for risk management within an organization, and with it, organizational culture.

clause: Management aligns the technical aspects of AI risk management to policies and operations.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The MAP function establishes the context to frame risks related to an AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The AI lifecycle consists of many interdependent activities involving a diverse set of actors (See Figure 3).

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: In practice, AI actors in charge of one part of the process often do not have full visibility or control over other parts their associated contexts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The interdependencies between these activities, and among the relevant AI actors, can make it difficult to reliably anticipate impacts of AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, early decisions in identifying purposes and objectives of an AI system can alter its behavior and capabilities, and the dynamics of deployment setting (such as end users or impacted individuals) can shape the impacts of AI system decisions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: As a result, the best intentions within one dimension of the AI lifecycle can be undermined via interactions with decisions and conditions in other, later activities.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The information gathered while carrying out the MAP function enables negative risk prevention and informs decisions for processes such as model management, as well as an initial decision about appropriateness or the need for an AI solution.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Outcomes in the MAP function are the basis for the MEASURE and MANAGE functions.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Without contextual knowledge, and awareness of risks within the identified contexts, risk management is difficult to perform.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The MAP function is intended to enhance an organization’s ability to identify risks and broader contributing factors.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Implementation of this function is enhanced by incorporating perspectives from a diverse internal team engagement with those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Engagement with external collaborators, end users, potentially impacted communities, and others may vary based on the risk level of a particular AI system, the makeup of the internal team, and organizational policies.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Gathering such broad perspectives can help organizations proactively prevent negative risks and develop more trustworthy AI systems by: identifying positive and beneficial uses of their existing AI systems

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: improving understanding of limitations in AI and ML processes

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: identifying known and foreseeable negative impacts related to intended use of AI systems

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: and anticipating risks of the use of AI systems beyond intended use.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: After completing the MAP function, Framework users should have sufficient contextual knowledge about AI system impacts to inform an initial go/no-go decision about whether to design, develop, or deploy an AI system.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: If a decision is made to proceed, organizations should utilize the MEASURE and MANAGE functions along with policies procedures put into place in the GOVERN function to assist in AI risk management efforts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: It is incumbent on Framework users to continue applying the MAP function to AI systems as context, capabilities, risks, benefits, and potential impacts evolve over time.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 6. AI RMF Profiles

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI RMF _use-case profiles_ are implementations of the AI RMF functions, categories, and subcategories for a specific setting or application based on the requirements, risk tolerance, and resources of the Framework user: for example, an AI RMF _hiring profile_ or an AI RMF _fair housing profile_ .

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Profiles may illustrate and offer insights into how risk can be managed at various stages of the AI lifecycle or in specific sector, technology, or end-use applications.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI RMF profiles assist organizations in deciding how they might best manage AI risk that is well-aligned with their goals, considers legal/regulatory requirements best practices, and reflects risk management priorities.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI RMF _temporal profiles_ are descriptions of either the current state or the desired, target state of specific AI risk management activities within a given sector, industry, organization, or application context. An AI RMF Current Profile indicates how AI is currently being managed the related risks in terms of current outcomes. A Target Profile indicates the outcomes needed to achieve the desired or target AI risk management goals.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Comparing Current

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Target Profiles likely reveals gaps to be addressed to meet AI risk management objectives.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Action plans can be developed to address these gaps to fulfill outcomes in a given category or subcategory.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Prioritization of gap mitigation is driven by the user’s needs risk management processes.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: This risk-based approach also enables Framework users to compare their approaches with other approaches and to gauge the resources needed (e.g., staffing, funding) to achieve AI risk management goals in a costeffective, prioritized manner.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI RMF _cross-sectoral profiles_ cover risks of models or applications that can be used across use cases or sectors. Cross-sectoral profiles can also cover how to govern, map, measure, and manage risks for activities or business processes common across sectors such as the use of large language models, cloud-based services or acquisition.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Tasks include articulating and documenting the system’s concept and objectives, underlying assumptions, context, and requirements; gathering and cleaning data; and documenting the metadata and characteristics of the dataset.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors in this category include data scientists, domain experts, socio-cultural analysts, experts in the field of diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility, members of impacted communities, human factors experts (e.g., UX/UI design), governance experts, data engineers, data providers, system funders, product managers, third-party entities, evaluators and legal and privacy governance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI Development tasks are performed during the AI Model phase of the lifecycle in Figure 2.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI Development actors provide the initial infrastructure of AI systems are responsible for model building and interpretation tasks, which involve the creation, selection, calibration, training, and/or testing of models or algorithms.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors in this category include machine learning experts, data scientists, developers, third-party entities, legal and privacy governance experts, and experts in the socio-cultural contextual factors associated with the deployment setting.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI Deployment tasks are performed during the Task

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Output phase of the lifecycle in Figure 2.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI Deployment actors are responsible for contextual decisions relating to how the AI system is used to assure deployment of the system into production.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Related tasks include piloting the system, checking compatibility with legacy systems ensuring regulatory compliance, managing organizational change, and evaluating user experience.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors in this category include system integrators, software developers, end users, operators and practitioners, evaluators, and domain experts with expertise in human factors, socio-cultural analysis, and governance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Operation and Monitoring tasks are performed in the Application Context/Operate and Monitor phase of the lifecycle in Figure 2.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These tasks are carried out by AI actors who are responsible for operating the AI system and working with others to regularly assess system output and impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors in this category include system operators, domain experts, AI designers, users who interpret or incorporate the output of AI systems, product developers, evaluators and auditors, compliance experts, organizational management, and members of the research community.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Test, Evaluation, Verification, and Validation (TEVV) tasks are performed throughout the AI lifecycle. They are carried out by AI actors who examine the AI system or its components, or detect and remediate problems. Ideally, AI actors carrying out verification

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human Factors tasks and activities are found throughout the dimensions of the AI lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: They include human-centered design practices and methodologies, promoting the active involvement of end users other interested parties relevant AI actors, incorporating context-specific norms and values in system design, evaluating and adapting end user experiences, and broad integration of humans and human dynamics in all phases of the AI lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human factors professionals provide multidisciplinary skills and perspectives to understand context of use, inform interdisciplinary and demographic diversity, engage in consultative processes, design and evaluate user experience, perform human-centered evaluation and testing and inform impact assessments.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Domain Expert tasks involve input from multidisciplinary practitioners or scholars who provide knowledge or expertise in – and about – an industry sector, economic sector, context, or application area where an AI system is being used. AI actors who are domain experts can provide essential guidance for AI system design and development, and interpret outputs in support of work performed by TEVV
