source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI Impact Assessment tasks include assessing and evaluating requirements for AI system accountability, combating harmful bias, examining impacts of AI systems, product safety, liability, and security, among others. AI actors such as impact assessors and evaluators provide technical, human factor, socio-cultural, and legal expertise.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Procurement tasks are conducted by AI actors with financial, legal, or policy management authority for acquisition of AI models, products, or services from a third-party developer, vendor, or contractor.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Governance

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Oversight tasks are assumed by AI actors with management, fiduciary, and legal authority and responsibility for the organization in which an AI system is de- signed, developed, and/or deployed. Key AI actors responsible for AI governance include organizational management, senior leadership, and the Board of Directors. These actors are parties that are concerned with the impact and sustainability of the organization as a whole.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Additional AI Actors

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Third-party entities include providers, developers, vendors, and evaluators of data, algorithms, models, and/or systems related services for another organization or the organization’s customers or clients.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Third-party entities are responsible for AI design development tasks, in whole or in part.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: By definition, they are external to the design, development, or deployment team of the organization that acquires its technologies or services.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The technologies acquired from third-party entities may be complex or opaque, and risk tolerances may not align with the deploying or operating organization.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: End users of an AI system are the individuals or groups that use the system for specific purposes. These individuals or groups interact with an AI system in a specific context. End users can range in competency from AI experts to first-time technology end users.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Affected individuals/communities encompass all individuals, groups, communities, or organizations directly or indirectly affected by AI systems or decisions based on the output of AI systems. These individuals do not necessarily interact with the deployed system or application.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Other AI actors may provide formal or quasi-formal norms or guidance for specifying and managing AI risks. They can include trade associations, standards developing organizations, advocacy groups, researchers, environmental groups, and civil society organizations .

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The general public is most likely to directly experience positive and negative impacts of AI technologies. They may provide the motivation for actions taken by the AI actors. This group can include individuals, communities and consumers associated with the context in which an AI system is developed or deployed.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Appendix B: How AI Risks Differ from Traditional Software Risks

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: As with traditional software, risks from AI-based technology can be bigger than an enterprise, span organizations, and lead to societal impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems also bring a set of risks that are not comprehensively addressed by current risk frameworks and approaches.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Some AI system features that present risks also can be beneficial.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: For example, pre-trained models and transfer learning can advance research and increase accuracy resilience when compared to other models and approaches.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Identifying contextual factors in the MAP function will assist AI actors in determining the level of risk potential management efforts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Compared to traditional software, AI-specific risks that are new or increased include the following:

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The data used for building an AI system may not be a true or appropriate representation of the context or intended use of the AI system, and the ground truth may either not exist or not be available. Additionally, harmful bias and other data quality issues can affect AI system trustworthiness, which could lead to negative impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI system dependency and reliance on data for training tasks, combined with increased volume complexity typically associated with such data.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Intentional or unintentional changes during training may fundamentally alter AI system performance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Datasets used to train AI systems may become detached from their original intended context or may become stale or outdated relative to deployment context.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI system scale and complexity (many systems contain billions or even trillions of decision points) housed within more traditional software applications.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Privacy risk due to enhanced data aggregation capability for AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems may require more frequent maintenance and triggers for conducting corrective maintenance due to data, model, or concept drift.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Underdeveloped software testing standards inability to document AI-based practices to the standard expected of traditionally engineered software for all but the simplest of cases.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Difficulty in performing regular AI-based software testing, or determining what to test, since AI systems are not subject to the same controls as traditional code development.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Computational costs for developing AI systems their impact on the environment and planet.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Inability to predict or detect the side effects of AI-based systems beyond statistical measures. cybersecurity risk management considerations and approaches are applicable in the design, development, deployment, evaluation, and use of AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Privacy and cybersecurity risks are also considered as part of broader enterprise risk management considerations, which may incorporate AI risks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: As part of the effort to address AI trustworthiness characteristics such as “Secure and Resilient” and “Privacy-Enhanced,” organizations may consider leveraging available standards guidance that provide broad guidance to organizations to reduce security and privacy risks

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework

clause: the NIST Cybersecurity Framework

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: the NIST Risk Management Framework, and the Secure Software Development Framework.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These frameworks have some features in common with the AI RMF.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Like most risk management approaches, they are outcome-based rather than prescriptive are often structured around a Core set of functions, categories, and subcategories.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: While there are significant differences between these frameworks based on the domain addressed – and because AI risk management calls for addressing many other types of risks – frameworks like those mentioned above may inform security and privacy considerations in the MAP , MEASURE and MANAGE functions of the AI RMF.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: At the same time, guidance available before publication of this AI RMF does not comprehensively address many AI system risks. For example, existing frameworks and guidance are unable to: adequately manage the problem of harmful bias in AI systems

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: confront the challenging risks related to generative AI

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: account for the complex attack surface of AI systems or other security abuses enabled by AI systems

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: and consider risks associated with third-party AI technologies, transfer learning, and offlabel use where AI systems may be trained for decision-making outside an organization’s security controls or trained in one domain then “fine-tuned” for another.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Both AI and traditional software technologies systems are subject to rapid innovation. Technology advances should be monitored deployed to take advantage of those developments and work towards a future of AI that is both trustworthy and responsible.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Appendix C: AI Risk Management and Human-AI Interaction

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Organizations that design, develop, or deploy AI systems for use in operational settings may enhance their AI risk management by understanding current limitations of humanAI interaction. The AI RMF provides opportunities to clearly define and differentiate the various human roles responsibilities when using, interacting with, or managing AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Many of the data-driven approaches that AI systems rely on attempt to convert or represent individual and social observational and decision-making practices into measurable quantities.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Representing complex human phenomena with mathematical models can come at the cost of removing necessary context.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: This loss of context may in turn make it difficult to understand individual. societal impacts that are key to AI risk management efforts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human roles and responsibilities in decision making and overseeing AI systems need to be clearly defined and differentiated.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Human-AI configurations can span from fully autonomous to fully manual.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI systems can autonomously make decisions, defer decision making to a human expert or be used by a human decision maker as an additional opinion.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Some AI systems may not require human oversight, such as models used to improve video compression.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Other systems may specifically require human oversight.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Decisions that go into the design, development, deployment, evaluation, and use of AI systems reflect systemic and human cognitive biases.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors bring their cognitive biases, both individual and group, into the process.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Biases can stem from end-user decision-making tasks be introduced across the AI lifecycle via human assumptions, expectations, and decisions during design and modeling tasks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These biases, which are not necessarily always harmful, may be exacerbated by AI system opacity and the resulting lack of transparency.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Systemic biases at the organizational level can influence how teams are structured and who controls the decision-making processes throughout the AI lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These biases can also influence downstream decisions by end users, decision makers, and policy makers may lead to negative impacts.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 3. Human-AI interaction results vary. Under certain conditions – for example

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: in perceptual-based judgment tasks – the AI part of the human-AI interaction can amplify human biases leading to more biased decisions than the AI or human alone. When these variations are judiciously taken into account in organizing human-AI teams, however, they can result in complementarity improved overall performance.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 4. Presenting AI system information to humans is complex. Humans perceive and derive meaning from AI system output explanations in different ways, reflecting different individual preferences, traits, and skills.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The GOVERN function provides organizations with the opportunity to clarify and define the roles and responsibilities for the humans in the Human-AI team configurations and those who are overseeing the AI system performance. The GOVERN function also creates mechanisms for organizations to make their decision-making processes more explicit, to help counter systemic biases.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The MAP function suggests opportunities to define document processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness concepts, and to define relevant technical standards and certifications.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Implementing MAP function categories and subcategories may help organizations improve their internal competency for analyzing context, identifying procedural and system limitations, exploring and examining impacts of AI-based systems in the real world and evaluating decision-making processes throughout the AI lifecycle.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The GOVERN and MAP functions describe the importance of interdisciplinarity and demographically diverse teams and utilizing feedback from potentially impacted individuals and communities.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI actors called out in the AI RMF who perform human factors tasks activities can assist technical teams by anchoring in design development practices to user intentions and representatives of the broader AI community, and societal values.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: These actors further help to incorporate context-specific norms and values in system design and evaluate end user experiences – in conjunction with AI systems.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: AI risk management approaches for human-AI configurations will be augmented by ongoing research and evaluation. For example, the degree to which humans are empowered incentivized to challenge AI system output requires further studies. Data about the frequency and rationale with which humans overrule AI system output in deployed systems may be useful to collect and analyze.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: Appendix D: Attributes of the AI RMF

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: NIST described several key attributes of the AI RMF when work on the Framework first began. These attributes have remained intact were used to guide the AI RMF’s development. They are provided here as a reference.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: The AI RMF strives to:

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 2. Be consensus-driven regularly updated through an open, transparent process. All stakeholders should have the opportunity to contribute to the AI RMF’s development.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 3. Use clear plain language that is understandable by a broad audience including senior executives, government officials, non-governmental organization leadership, and those who are not AI professionals – while still of sufficient technical depth to be useful to practitioners. The AI RMF should allow for communication of AI risks across an organization

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: between organizations

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: with customers, and to the public at large.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 4. Provide common language and understanding to manage AI risks. The AI RMF should offer taxonomy, terminology, definitions, metrics, and characterizations for AI risk.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 5. Be easily usable fit well with other aspects of risk management. Use of the Framework should be intuitive and readily adaptable as part of an organization’s broader risk management strategy and processes. It should be consistent or aligned with other approaches to managing AI risks.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 6. Be useful to a wide range of perspectives, sectors, and technology domains. The AI RMF should be universally applicable to any AI technology and to context-specific use cases.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 8. Take advantage of and foster greater awareness of existing standards, guidelines, best practices, methodologies, and tools for managing AI risks – as well as illustrate the need for additional improved resources.

source_full: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
clause: 10. Be a living document. The AI RMF should be readily updated as technology, understanding, and approaches to AI trustworthiness and uses of AI change and as stakeholders learn from implementing AI risk management generally and this framework in particular.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Winning the Race_ AMERICA’S AI ACTION PLAN

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AMERICA’S AI ACTION PLAN

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The United States is in a race to achieve global dominance in artificial intelligence (AI).

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Whoever has the largest AI ecosystem will set global AI standards and reap broad economic and military benefits.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Just like we won the space race, it is imperative that the United States and its allies win this race.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: President Trump took decisive steps toward achieving this goal during his first days in office by signing Executive Order 14179, “Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence,” calling for America to retain dominance in this global race and directing the creation of an AI Action Plan.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Winning the AI race will usher in a new golden age of human flourishing, economic competitiveness, and national security for the American people.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI will enable Americans to discover new materials, synthesize new chemicals, manufacture new drugs, and develop new methods to harness energy—an industrial revolution.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: It will enable radically new forms of education, media, and communication—an information revolution.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: And it will enable altogether new intellectual achievements: unraveling ancient scrolls once thought unreadable, making breakthroughs in scientific and mathematical theory, and creating new kinds of digital and physical art—a _renaissance_ .

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: An industrial revolution, an information revolution, and a renaissance—all at once. This is the potential that AI presents. The opportunity that stands before us is both inspiring and humbling. And it is ours to seize, or to lose.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: America’s AI Action Plan has three pillars: innovation, infrastructure, and international diplomacy and security.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The United States needs to innovate faster and more comprehensively than our competitors in the development and distribution of new AI technology across every field, and dismantle unnecessary regulatory barriers that hinder the private sector in doing so.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: As Vice President Vance remarked at the Paris AI Action Summit in February, restricting AI development with onerous regulation “would not only unfairly benefit incumbents… it would mean paralyzing one of the most promising technologies we have seen in generations.”

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: That is why President Trump rescinded the Biden Administration’s dangerous actions on day one.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: We need to build maintain vast AI infrastructure and the energy to power it. To do that, we will continue to reject radical climate dogma bureaucratic red tape, as the Administration has done since Inauguration Day. Simply put, we need to “Build, Baby, Build!”

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: We need to establish American AI—from our advanced semiconductors to our models to our applications—as the gold standard for AI worldwide and ensure our allies are building on American technology.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Pillar I: Accelerate AI Innovation

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: America must have the most powerful AI systems in the world, but we must also lead the world in creative and transformative application of these systems. Achieving these goals requires the Federal government to create the conditions where private-sector-led innovation can flourish.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: To maintain global leadership in AI, America’s private sector must be unencumbered by bureaucratic red tape.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: President Trump has already taken multiple steps toward this goal including rescinding Biden Executive Order 14110 on AI that foreshadowed an onerous regulatory regime.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI is far too important to smother in bureaucracy at this early stage, whether at the state or Federal level.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The Federal government should not allow AI-related Federal funding to be directed toward states with burdensome AI regulations that waste these funds but should also not interfere with states’ rights to pass prudent laws that are not unduly restrictive to innovation.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), launch a Request for Information from businesses the public at large about current Federal regulations that hinder AI innovation and adoption, and work with relevant Federal agencies to take appropriate action.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by the Office of Management

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by OMB, work with Federal agencies that have AI-related discretionary funding programs to ensure, consistent with applicable law, that they consider a state’s AI regulatory climate when making funding decisions limit funding if the state’s AI regulatory regimes may hinder the effectiveness of that funding or award.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Review all Federal Trade Commission (FTC) investigations commenced under the previous administration to ensure that they do not advance theories of liability that unduly burden AI innovation. Furthermore, review all FTC final orders, consent decrees, and injunctions, and, where appropriate, seek to modify or set-aside any that unduly burden AI innovation.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Ensure that Frontier AI Protects Free Speech and American Values_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI systems will play a profound role in how we educate our children, do our jobs and consume media. It is essential that these systems be built from the ground up with freedom of speech and expression in mind and that U.S. government policy does not interfere with that objective. We must ensure that free speech flourishes in the era of AI that AI procured by the Federal government objectively reflects truth rather than social engineering agendas.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by the Department of Commerce (DOC) through the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), revise the NIST AI Risk Management Framework to eliminate references to misinformation, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, and climate change.[ 6]

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by DOC through NIST’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI), conduct research and, as appropriate, publish evaluations of frontier models from the People’s Republic of China for alignment with Chinese Communist Party talking points and censorship.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: They also benefit commercial government adoption of AI because many businesses and governments have sensitive data that they cannot send to closed model vendors.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Enable AI Adoption_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Today, the bottleneck to harnessing AI’s full potential is not necessarily the availability of models, tools, or applications.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Rather, it is the limited and slow adoption of AI, particularly within large established organizations.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Many of America’s most critical sectors, such as healthcare, are especially slow to adopt due to a variety of factors including distrust or lack of understanding of the technology, a complex regulatory landscape, and a lack of clear governance and risk mitigation standards.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: A coordinated Federal effort would be beneficial in establishing a dynamic, “try-first” culture for AI across American industry.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Establish regulatory sandboxes or AI Centers of Excellence around the country where researchers, startups, and established enterprises can rapidly deploy test AI tools while committing to open sharing of data and results. These efforts would be enabled by regulatory agencies such as the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by the Department of Defense (DOD) in coordination with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), regularly update joint DOD-Intelligence Community (IC) assessments of the comparative level of adoption of AI tools by the United States, its competitors and its adversaries’ national security establishments and establish an approach for continuous adaptation of the DOD and IC’s respective AI adoption initiatives based on these AI net assessments.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Prioritize, collect, and distribute intelligence on foreign frontier AI projects that may have national security implications, via collaboration between the IC, the Department of Energy (DOE), CAISI at DOC, the National Security Council (NSC), and OSTP.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The Trump Administration supports a worker-first AI agenda.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: By accelerating productivity and creating entirely new industries, AI can help America build an economy that delivers more pathways to economic opportunity for American workers.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: But it will also transform how work gets done across all industries and occupations, demanding a serious workforce response to help workers navigate that transition.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The Trump Administration has already taken significant steps to lead on this front including the April 2025 Executive Orders 14277 and 14278, “Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth” and “Preparing Americans for High-Paying Skilled Trade Jobs of the Future.”[7, 8] To continue delivering on this vision

clause: Led by DOL, leverage available discretionary funding, where appropriate, to fund rapid retraining for individuals impacted by AI-related job displacement.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Issue clarifying guidance to help states identify eligible dislocated workers in sectors undergoing significant structural change tied to AI adoption, as well as guidance clarifying how state Rapid Response funds can be used to proactively upskill workers at risk of future displacement.

clause: At DOL and DOC, rapidly pilot new approaches to workforce challenges created by AI, which may include areas such as rapid retraining needs driven by worker displacement and shifting skill requirements for entry-level roles.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI will enable a wide range of new innovations in the physical world: autonomous drones, selfdriving cars, robotics, and other inventions for which terminology does not yet exist.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: It is crucial that America our trusted allies be world-class manufacturers of these next-generation technologies.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI, robotics, and related technologies create opportunities for novel capabilities in manufacturing and logistics including ones with applications to defense and national security.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The Federal government should prioritize investment in these emerging technologies and usher in a new industrial renaissance.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Invest in AI-Enabled Science_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Like many other domains, science itself will be transformed by AI.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI systems can already generate models of protein structures, novel materials, and much else.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Increasingly powerful general-purpose models show promise in formulating hypotheses and designing experiments.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: These nascent capabilities promise to accelerate scientific advancement.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: They will only do so, however, with critical changes in the way science is conducted including the enabling scientific infrastructure.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI-enabled predictions are of little use if scientists cannot also increase the scale of experimentation.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Basic science today is often a labor-intensive process; the AI era will require more scientific and engineering research to transform theories into industrial-scale enterprises.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: This, in turn, will necessitate new infrastructure support of new kinds of scientific organizations.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Through NSF, DOE, NIST at DOC, and other Federal partners, invest in automated cloud-enabled labs for a range of scientific fields including engineering, materials science, chemistry, biology, and neuroscience, built by, as appropriate, the private sector, Federal agencies, and research institutions in coordination and collaboration with DOE National Laboratories.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Use long-term agreements to support Focused-Research Organizations or other similar entities using AI and other emerging technologies to make fundamental scientific advancements.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Require federally funded researchers to disclose non-proprietary, non-sensitive datasets that are used by AI models during the course of research and experimentation.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: High-quality data has become a national strategic asset as governments pursue AI innovation goals and capitalize on the technology’s economic benefits. Other countries including our adversaries, have raced ahead of us in amassing vast troves of scientific data. The United States must lead the creation of the world’s largest highest quality AI-ready scientific datasets

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: while maintaining respect for individual rights and ensuring civil liberties, privacy, and confidentiality protections.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Direct the National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) Machine Learning and AI Subcommittee to make recommendations on minimum data quality standards for the use of biological, materials science, chemical, physical, and other scientific data modalities in AI model training. ultimately facilitating the improved use of AI for evidence building by statistical agencies while protecting confidential data from inappropriate access and use.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Establish secure compute environments within NSF and DOE to enable secure AI usecases for controlled access to restricted Federal data.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Create an online portal for NSF’s National Secure Data Service (NSDS) demonstration project to provide the public and Federal agencies with a front door to AI use-cases involving controlled access to restricted Federal data.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Advance the Science of AI_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Just as LLMs and generative AI systems represented a paradigm shift in the science of AI, future breakthroughs may similarly transform what is possible with AI. It is imperative that the United States remain the leading pioneer of such breakthroughs and this begins with strategic, targeted investment in the most promising paths at the frontier.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Prioritize investment in theoretical, computational, and experimental research to preserve America’s leadership in discovering new transformative paradigms that advance the capabilities of AI, reflecting this priority in the forthcoming National AI R&D Strategic Plan.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Invest in AI Interpretability, Control, and Robustness Breakthroughs_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Today, the inner workings of frontier AI systems are poorly understood.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Technologists know how LLMs work at a high level, but often cannot explain why a model produced a specific output.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: This can make it hard to predict the behavior of any specific AI system.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: This lack of predictability, in turn, can make it challenging to use advanced AI in defense, national security, or other applications where lives are at stake.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The United States will be better able to use AI systems to their fullest potential in high-stakes national security domains if we make fundamental breakthroughs on these research problems.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Launch a technology development program led by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency in collaboration with CAISI at DOC and NSF, to advance AI interpretability, AI control systems, and adversarial robustness.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Prioritize fundamental advancements in AI interpretability, control, and robustness as part of the forthcoming National AI R&D Strategic Plan.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: The DOD, DOE, CAISI at DOC, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), NSF, and academic partners should coordinate an AI hackathon initiative to solicit the best brightest from U.S. academia to test AI systems for transparency, effectiveness, use control, and security vulnerabilities.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Build an AI Evaluations Ecosystem_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Evaluations are how the AI industry assesses the performance and reliability of AI systems. Rigorous evaluations can be a critical tool in defining and measuring AI reliability performance in regulated industries. Over time, regulators should explore the use of evaluations in their application of existing law to AI systems.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Publish guidelines resources through NIST at DOC including CAISI, for Federal agencies to conduct their own evaluations of AI systems for their distinct missions and operations and for compliance with existing law.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Support the development of the science of measuring and evaluating AI models led by NIST at DOC, DOE, NSF, and other Federal science agencies.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Convene meetings at least twice per year under the auspices of CAISI at DOC for Federal agencies and the research community to share learnings best practices on building AI evaluations.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Invest, via DOE and NSF, in the development of AI testbeds for piloting AI systems in secure, real-world settings, allowing researchers to prototype new AI systems and translate them to the market.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Such testbeds would encourage participation by broad multistakeholder teams and span a wide variety of economic verticals touched by AI. including agriculture, transportation, and healthcare delivery.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Led by DOC, convene the NIST AI Consortium to empower the collaborative establishment of new measurement science that will enable the identification of proven, scalable, and interoperable techniques and metrics to promote the development of AI.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: _Accelerate AI Adoption in Government_

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: With AI tools in use, the Federal government can serve the public with far greater efficiency and effectiveness. Use cases include accelerating slow often manual internal processes, streamlining public interactions, and many others. Taken together, transformative use of AI can help deliver the highly responsive government the American people expect and deserve.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: OMB has already advanced AI adoption in government by reducing onerous rules imposed by the Biden Administration.[17, 18] Now is the time to build on this success.

clause: Formalize the Chief Artificial Intelligence Officer Council (CAIOC) as the primary venue for interagency coordination and collaboration on AI adoption. Through the CAIOC, initiate strategic coordination collaboration with relevant Federal executive councils

clause: to include: the President’s Management Council, Chief Data Officer Council, Chief Information Officer Council, Interagency Council on Statistical Policy, Chief Human Capital Officer Council, and Federal Privacy Council.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Create a talent-exchange program designed to allow rapid details of Federal staff to other agencies in need of specialized AI talent (e.g., data scientists and software engineers), with input from the Office of Personnel Management.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Create an AI procurement toolbox managed by the General Services Administration (GSA), in coordination with OMB, that facilitates uniformity across the Federal enterprise to the greatest extent practicable.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: This system would allow any Federal agency to easily choose among multiple models in a manner compliant with relevant privacy, data governance, and transparency laws.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Agencies should also have ample flexibility to customize models to their own ends, as well as to see a catalog of other agency AI uses (based on OMB’s pre-existing AI Use Case Inventory).

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Implement an Advanced Technology Transfer and Capability Sharing Program with GSA to quickly transfer advanced AI capabilities use cases between agencies.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Convene, under the auspices of OMB, a cohort of agencies with High Impact Service Providers to pilot and increase the use of AI to improve the delivery of services to the public.

clause: Establish an AI & Autonomous Systems Virtual Proving Ground at DOD, beginning with scoping the technical, geographic, security, and resourcing requirements necessary for such a facility.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Develop a streamlined process within DOD for classifying, evaluating and optimizing workflows involved in its major operational and enabling functions, aiming to develop a list of priority workflows for automation with AI. When a workflow is successfully automated

clause: DOD should strive to permanently transition that workflow to the AI-based implementation as quickly as practicable.

clause: Grow our Senior Military Colleges into hubs of AI research, development, and talent building, teaching core AI skills and literacy to future generations. clause: Pillar II: Build American AI Infrastructure

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: AI is the first digital service in modern life that challenges America to build vastly greater energy generation than we have today. American energy capacity has stagnated since the 1970s while China has rapidly built out their grid. America’s path to AI dominance depends on changing this troubling trend.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: Like most general-purpose technologies of the past, AI will require new infrastructure— factories to produce chips, data centers to run those chips and new sources of energy to power it all. America’s environmental permitting system and other regulations make it almost impossible to build this infrastructure in the United States with the speed that is required. Additionally

clause: this infrastructure must also not be built with any adversarial technology that could undermine U.S. AI dominance.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: To build the infrastructure needed to power America’s AI future, we must also invest in the workforce that will build, operate, and maintain it—including roles such as electricians, advanced HVAC technicians, and a host of other high-paying occupations.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
clause: To address the shortages in many of these critical jobs, the Trump Administration should identify the priority roles that underpin AI infrastructure, develop modern skills frameworks, support industrydriven training and expand early pipelines through general education, CTE and Registered Apprenticeships to fuel American AI leadership.

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan

source_full: Winning the Race: America's AI Action Plan
